primary.title: How SQM Turned a 678 km² Mine into an Autonomous Inspection Zone
primary.why_strongest_fit: This case study is about the lead's own company. SQM already runs DJI Dock-based autonomous inspection on FlytBase across a 678 km² operation in the Atacama Desert, the same desert, country and kind of operation as Rodrigo Castillo's 3 lithium sites. It shows manual field inspection (engineers walking or driving kilometers under the desert sun) being replaced by daily autonomous missions, which maps directly to his goal of replacing expensive, hazardous contracted crews. It also names the local integrator (Adentu) and the data pipeline (FlytBase to Azure) that SQM has already approved internally, which lowers technical and procurement risk before the Q3 budget conversation. Expanding from an existing internal success to the Northern Operations Division is a far stronger argument than any outside reference.
key_proof_points: SQM "cut inspection time from days to hours"
"improved iodine extraction yield by two percent"
678 km² mining operation in northern Chile (Atacama Desert)
"It was the first time SQM's inspection team could start their day with a ranked list of priorities generated entirely by autonomous systems."
primary.how_to_use_it: Open with the internal proof point: 'Your colleagues on SQM's Digital Innovation team (Rodrigo Toler) already run FlytBase with Adentu across 678 km² in the Atacama.' Position the Northern Operations request as scaling a proven internal programme to 3 more 24/7 sites, not a new pilot. Ask whether he knows the Digital Innovation team and offer an introduction or joint call with Adentu. Use the >95% reliability, days-to-hours and doubled-frequency metrics in the Q3 budget business case. Note the page headline says '4× iodine yield' while the body says a two percent improvement, so quote the body text.

secondary.title: How Anglo American Uses Autonomous Drones to Transform Mining Safety in Peru
secondary.why: This is the referrer's own FlytBase deployment: drone-in-a-box at the Quellaveco copper mine in Peru with LATAM partner UAV LATAM. It replaced manual drone flights and truck travel across inaccessible, mountainous terrain to cut travel time and personnel safety exposure. Use it to acknowledge the referral and as a peer LATAM mining reference for safety and remote-site connectivity (elevated dock placement).

referral_connection.explanation: FlytBase's site has an Anglo American case study. Anglo American deployed FlytBase-powered drone-in-a-box technology at its Quellaveco copper mine in Peru through implementation partner UAV LATAM. The deployment replaced manual drone flights and truck transport between survey locations, improving personnel safety in mountainous terrain, and the case study frames it as a new standard for mining safety in Latin America. The likely referral path is a mining peer who has seen autonomous docks working in LATAM.

existing_relationship.explanation: Yes. SQM partnered with Chile-based integrator Adentu and FlytBase to automate inspection across its 678 km² operation in northern Chile. It started as a single-DJI-Dock pilot detecting irrigation leaks and leaching inefficiencies and grew into a daily automated inspection ecosystem, with RGB and thermal imagery feeding SQM's Azure ML environment. Reported results: inspection time from days to hours, >95% mission reliability, doubled inspection frequency and a 2% iodine extraction yield improvement. The case study names Rodrigo Toler (Deputy Manager of Digital Innovation, SQM). The inbound lead comes from a different person and division (Rodrigo Castillo, Northern Operations Division) and does not mention this, so treat it as account expansion and coordinate with the existing account owner and Adentu.
